Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova, et amplissima collectio ... quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi evulgavit. Tomus Sextus: ab anno CCCCXLI ad annum CCCCLI inclusive
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction for H. Welter, Paris and Leipzig, of the Florence edition 'expensis Antonii Zatta Veneti'
Publication Date: 1901 (the facsimile: 'Editio iterata ad Editionis principis exemplum ab Huberto Welter ... Parisiis M.D.CCCCI' at file line 164; 'H. WELTER' at 87; the original edition is catalogued by archive.org as 1761)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: the 1901 facsimile date is printed at file line 164; the underlying edition is of the 18th century); the item record carries no rights field
Language: lat (Latin, with the Greek of the conciliar acts printed in parallel; the OCR renders the long s as f and recovers the Greek column only in part)
Source: archive.org item sacrorumconcilio0006joan (catalogue title 'SACRORUM CONCILIORUM', volume 6, catalogue date 1761, contributor Internet Archive), full text at https://archive.org/download/sacrorumconcilio0006joan/sacrorumconcilio0006joan_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-10-17 by the Shared-Events source-research thread (Era 2 worker D); the byte count of the downloaded file (3,631,823) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: the 1901 facsimile date read in the OCR of the title page places the printing out of US copyright under this project's pd-us-by-date rule; the text reproduced is that of the 1761 edition, older still.
Content note: Mansi tomus 6, 441 to 451 (span at file line 145): the Eutychian controversy and the first sessions of Chalcedon. Leo's letters of 449-451 including the Tome to Flavian (noted at 91406), a Constantinopolitan council of 440-444 (44993), and 'CONCILIUM CHALCEDONENSE' (heading 784) with 'ACTIO PRIMA' at 53711, inside which the acts of Ephesus II (449) are read back into the record ('EPHESI ACTA SUB DIOSCORO', 77925), and within them the acts of Flavian's Home Synod of 448 against Eutyches (no separate heading located by search; they sit inside the first session). The editors' note at 14481 on the obscure phrase about Euphemia in Leo's correspondence, 'from which the story told by Zonaras and later Greeks is believed to have arisen', is the earliest critical comment held on the Euphemia-tomb legend. Latin and Greek primary documents of Chalcedon, sessions I-III.
